## Introduction

In these exercises, you'll practice with creating and pushing to GitHub repositories,
and with using software at OSC.

#### Setting up

- Start a VS Code session through OSC OnDemand in the folder `/fs/ess/PAS2880/$USER`.

## Exercise 1: GitHub

1. Go to the GitHub website, log in, and create a new GitHub repository.
   This  will be the remote counterpart of the Git repo you made as
   part of last week's assignment.
   You can give the GitHub repo any name you want.

2. In the terminal in VS Code, navigate to your dir for last week's assigmment.
   Then, use Git commands to set up a connection between the Git repo
   and the GitHub counterpart.
   
3. Push your local repo to the online counterpart.

4. Explore your repo on GitHub.
   Does your `README.md` render well? Can you see all your commits?

5. Open a GitHub Issue for your repo:
   on the GitHub page for your repo, in the Issues tab, click "New Issue",
   and in the box where you can type your issue, tag the instructor.
   For example:
    
   ```markdown
   Hey @jelmerp, can you please take a look at my repo?
   ```

   _(You will use this approach to "hand in" the remaining assignments for this course.)_
   
6. Back in VS Code, add a line to your `README.md` that mentions you created a
   Github repo on today's date, adding the repo's URL.

7. Commit the change to `README.md` to your Git repo.

8. Push to the remote and check that the changes were applied in the online repo.

## Exercise 2: Modules and Pandoc

_(In the shell, you should remain in the dir for last week's assignment.)_

We'll practice with modules and `pandoc`,
the program that can, among others, render Markdown files to HTML and PDF.

1. Check if Pandoc is available, and if so, which version, by running `pandoc -v`.

2. Use Google (or something similar) to check whether that Pandoc version appears
   to be the most recent one.
   
3. Check whether a more recent Pandoc version is available in an OSC Lmod module.

4. Load the OSC module with the most recent available Pandoc version.

5. Use Pandoc to create a PDF of your `README.md`. The command to do so is:
   
   ```bash
   pandoc -o README.pdf README.md
   ```

6. Was a PDF file created?

7. To view PDF files in VS Code, you'll first need to install an extension.
   Install the extension "Papyrus PDF Preview", and then take a look at your PDF.
   
8. Download the PDF file to your computer and also take a look at it there.

## Exercise 3: containers

1. Go to <https://seqera.io/containers> and find a container image for the program
   called "Trim-Galore".
   _(This program trims and filters FASTQ files, and you'll use it in the next_
   _few weeks of the course.)_

2. Back in VS Code, test-run the container with the command `trim_galore -v`.

## Solutions

### Exercise 1

<details><summary>**2.** Navigate, then set up a connection to the online repo</summary>

```bash
cd GA2

# (replace <SSH-URL-to-repo> with your actual SSH (not HTTPS!) URL)
git remote add origin <SSH-URL-to-repo>
```

</details>

<details><summary>**3.** Push your local repo to the online one you just created</summary>

When you push to a remote repo for the first time,
you need to add the `-u origin main` part:

```bash
git push -u origin main
```
</details>

<details><summary>**7.** Commit the change you made to `README.md`</summary>

```bash
git add README.md
git commit -m "Update README with GitHub repo information"
```
</details>

<details><summary>**8.** Push to the remote</summary>

Since you've pushed to this remote before, a simple `git push` works:

```bash
git push
```
</details>

### Exercise 2

<details><summary>**1.** Check if Pandoc is available, and if so, which version, by running `pandoc -v`</summary>

As of September 2025, the version is `2.14.0.3`:
  
```bash
pandoc -v
```
```bash-out
pandoc 2.14.0.3
Compiled with pandoc-types 1.22.1, texmath 0.12.3.3, skylighting 0.10.5.2,
citeproc 0.4.0.1, ipynb 0.1.0.1
User data directory: /users/PAS0471/jelmer/.local/share/pandoc
Copyright (C) 2006-2021 John MacFarlane. Web:  https://pandoc.org
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions. There is no
warranty, not even for merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose.
```
</details>

<details><summary>**2.** Check whether this appears to be the most recent version of Pandoc</summary>
Version 2.14 is [not nearly the most recent one](https://pandoc.org/releases.html),
which is 3.8 as of September 2025.
</p></details>

<details><summary>**3.** Is a more recent Pandoc version available in an OSC module?</summary>

Yes:
   
```bash
module spider pandoc
```
```bash-out
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  pandoc:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Versions:
        pandoc/2.19.2
        pandoc/3.6.4
```
</details>

<details><summary>**4.** Load the module with the most recent available Pandoc version</summary>

```bash
module load pandoc/3.6.4

pandoc -v
```
```bash-out
pandoc 3.6.4
Features: +server +lua
Scripting engine: Lua 5.4
User data directory: /users/PAS0471/jelmer/.local/share/pandoc
Copyright (C) 2006-2024 John MacFarlane. Web: https://pandoc.org
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions. There is no
warranty, not even for merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose.
```
</details>
   
<details><summary>**6.** Was a PDF file created?</summary>

If all went well, Pandoc did not print anything to screen,
but the PDF file should be there:

```bash
ls
```
```bash-out
data    README.md   README.pdf    results
```

</details>

<details><summary>**7.** Install the Papyrus PDF Preview and open the file.</summary>

1. Click on the Extensions icons (four squares) in the narrow side bar to open 
   the Extensions panel in the wide side bar.

2. Search for "papyrus" (or similar) and the extension should pop up:

![](../img/vscode_pdf-extension.png){width="60%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="A screenshot of the search result for the Papyrus PDF Preview VS Code extension."}

3. Click "Install".

4. After installation, you should be able to open the PDF file e.g. by simply
   clicking on it in the VS Code file explorer.

</details>

<details><summary>**8.** Download the PDF file</summary>

- Recall that in the VS Code file explorer, you can right-click on a file and
  select "Download..." to download a file to your computer.
  
- Alternatively, you could do this in the OnDemand file explorer.

</details>
